frontier_hypothesis.text: Attention and operational criteria may jointly constrain Integrated Information Theory, so relieving one may shift the bottleneck to the other.

frontier_hypothesis.falsification_test: Relieve Attention alone while measuring Integrated Information Theory. The hypothesis fails if Integrated Information Theory keeps improving without operational criteria becoming the binding limit, or if relieving operational criteria alone has no effect.
frontier_hypothesis.assumptions: Assumes each cited relation holds in the same setting and that effects carry across the shared term. It also assumes that terms with the same head noun name the same quantity.

co_mentions.quote: Throughout, I will pay particular attention to Integrated Information Theory (IIT) which provides the deepest explanation for consciousness at the causal level, while still failing to resolve the hard problem.
# The Integrated Information Theory needs Attention

support.quote: Thus, with the partial exception of the most radical panpsychist formulations (“everything is conscious”), virtually all differentiating theories ultimately require operational criteria.

setups.quote: Ultimately, conscious uptake is controlled by attention (Posner 1994).
In this review, we compare and contrast three theories being investigated in one such adversarial collaboration: Integrated Information Theory, Neurorepresentationalism, and Active Inference.

While theories like Global Workspace Theory (GWT) [Baars, 1988, Dehaene and Changeux, 2011], Integrated Information Theory (IIT) [Tononi, 2004, Oizumi et al., 2014], and Higher-Order Theories (HOT) [Rosenthal, 2005, Lau and Rosenthal, 2011] propose distinct neural signatures of awareness (ranging from non-linear “ignition” [Dehaene, 2014] and causal integration (Φ) [Oizumi et al., 2014] to metacognitive self-monitoring [Fleming et al., 2010]), testing them in biological systems is constrained by the inability to perform precise architectural ablations.

citation.quote: Most neuroscientific and cognitive theories, including GWT, HOT, LRT, AST rely on neural-behavioral co-occurrence as evidence.
citation.subject: neural behavioral co

steps: Run all four combinations of low and high Attention and operational criteria; measure Integrated Information Theory.
Hold neural behavioral co fixed or record them as covariates.
Compare the joint effect with the sum of the separate effects.
test_plan.fails_if: Neither Attention nor operational criteria moves Integrated Information Theory, or their joint effect equals the sum of the separate effects (no interaction or shifting bottleneck).
